utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if you'd like to take a seat. Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Naumovski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Buntic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you first of all just tell us your full name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Buntic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, you prepared this outline which we have provided to the Trial Chamber and the opposite bench but you have compiled also a different outline which had about 100 paragraphs and 27 pages?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The outline which we have provided to the Trial Chamber is a summary of your previous outline?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it only contains the essential elements from the previous ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the more comprehensive outlines which you have prepared, we have omitted all the parts which the Trial Chamber has already had enough opportunity to hear about the historical and political.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the analytical part, the -- including the legislature, legislation such as the constitution and the defence law?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are married, you have five children and you are a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. And two of those are only 15 days old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You graduated in Ljubuski on statement in courtroom in Bosnia-Herzegovina from high school and you completed the school of law in Zagreb where you graduated in 1978?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I graduated in 1978 and following that, I worked in Citluk in three different companies in the period between 1978 and 1988. Between 1989 and 1992 when the war broke out, I had my own law practice in Citluk and after the war, I assumed new duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between 1990 and April 1992, you were a member of the Croatian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the Croatian Democratic Party between 1990 and 1992. I also should point out that I was never a member of the HDZ either the HDZ-BiH or the HDZ in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summer of 1991, the local municipal assembly in Citluk appointed you as one of the members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was immediately following the crisis after the tanks were stopped at Siroki Brijeg, more precisely in Polog. And the crisis staffs were set up everywhere in western Herzegovina, and I was a member of the Crisis Staff in Citluk, and I was also there as a member of -- as a representative of the other political party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to this duty as member of the municipal Crisis Staff, between March and May 1991, you were the deputy commander of the brigade of the battalion which held the line?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was deputy commander of this battalion which was deployed in the Neretva River Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was an HVO battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were then asked to become a head of the justice department in the newly formed civil HVO in Citluk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had spoken to Mr. Mate Boban who came to -- who had come to Citluk and offered me this position and it is true that I was appointed by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to be the head of justice department in the civilian HVO, but it is also true that I never assumed this duty right away, but rather stayed with my Brotnjo battalion until the 26th of August until the area between Mostar and Stolac was liberated. So I really only assumed the duty of head of the justice department, I took it on -- after August 26th even though the appointment formally started on -- around the 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, if you can just wait a little bit with your response because we need to have all your answers interpreted. And just one more question. Mr. Boban signed the letter of appointment of you as the head of justice department?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also a member of the personnel commission of the HVO, and Mr. Dario Kordic was a member, also a member of this commission. This commission was established on 18 November 1991 [as interpreted], and Dr. Jadranko Prlic, president of the HVO, signed this decision?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, the president of this commission was Mr. Vladimir Soljic. I also am not aware of the fact that this commission ever met. I'm not aware of any decision that it ever adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one additional follow-up question. Your department and other departments appointed deputies and other officials independently or through this commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: This commission was never consulted, and as far as the executive part of the HVO is concerned, the heads of these departments were offered certain proposals. They went to the HD HB meetings and they would then confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one correction for the record. You referred to 18 November 1992, and the record reflects 1991.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then in December 1993 you were elected the president of the HR HB Judicial Council?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was in this duty between December 1993 and August 1996, that is, until this body was dissolved. And I continue to -- and now I have my own law office in Mostar, Buntic & Associates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We will now move to your time line and beginnings of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. First we will deal with the heading called "Prelude," paragraphs 9 and 10, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, there is no need to deal with paragraphs 9 and 10, which are a matter of history. You can deal briefly with paragraphs 11 and 12. Again, these are matters of history. There's no need for any lengthy evidence on those. And move on, if you would, to page 3 as quickly as you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We will move swiftly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, a couple of questions regarding the quiet occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, if we can call it that way. After the beginning of the war in Croatia and Slovenia, the JNA transferred or moved all its arsenals from Slovenia and Croatia to Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the conclusion of the war in Slovenia, all military equipment was moved to Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then at the end of 1991 the JNA moved out of Croatia and was strategically deployed in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And Sarajevo, as the capital of Bosnia-Herzegovina, became cut off from the other centres: Banja Luka, Tuzla, Mostar, Zenica. The communications were cut off. And I would like to say that this was a quiet occupation, whereby about 70 to 75 per cent of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina was occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, Their Honours have heard a lot about the events at Ravno. We will not dwell on it. You pointed out in paragraph 12 that for you in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the war began in September 18, 1991, when the JNA captured the strategically important Dubravska plateau in the municipality of Stolac, from where the attacks were then launched on Ravno and Zlatina and Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Somewhere around the 18th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need to go into this in detail. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. A couple of words on the political misunderstandings towards the end of 1991. Your Honours, we prepared a bundle of eight documents which we will use in the examination of Mr. Buntic, and I would like to tender them now and then we will refer to them later.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D279/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, I would just like to ask you a couple of questions about this political misunderstanding in 1991. After the constitutional changes in July of 1990, the Bosnian Croats were in a precarious condition, constitutionally speaking. They had no possibility to adopt their own decisions because a two-third majority was needed. So either alone or in alliance with the Muslims, they were not able to affect constitutional changes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 31st of July, amendments to the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina were adopted, and the constitutional changes were only possible if two-thirds of the both houses of parliament voted for it. And without two-thirds majority, no constitutional changes could be adopted. And the constitution had to be adopted at that time, because up until then there was a single-party system, a communist system, and no changes could be introduced, because the assembly could not reach a two-thirds majority on any decision. That is, the SDS blocked and obstructed both houses of the BiH parliament. It also obstructed the work of the assembly and the presidency. Croats were in an especially awkward position because they had no majority. They could not prevent changes or effect changes. And even together with other ethnic groups, they could not do so. That means that short of consensus, they could not effect any rights. Muslims or Serbs could do so, but Croats could not do it, either alone or with Serbs or Croats. That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you Mr. Buntic, not out of discourtesy but as you will appreciate, we've heard a very great deal of evidence in the last 16 months in this trial and there is much that we know about. It's also important that witnesses just deal as concisely as possible with the questions that they are asked. So could you concentrate on the question and then answer it as briefly as possible and we will be able to finish your evidence, of course, more quickly and you will be able to get away. Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, just as a reminder, in Tab 1 of this bundle we have provided are the amendments which we have just referred to. We need not go through them individually; they speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on. This is the formation of the ad hoc Crisis Staffs. According to the laws and individual statutes in municipalities, it was provided that in the case of immediate threat of war which may result from an outside aggression, the municipal assemblies would be dissolved, abandoned and their roles would be taken over by the War Presidencies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in the specific case something else happened, the occupation was conducted by the -- carried out by the JNA which at that time was the only legal military organisation in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. In other words, this was not a foreign aggression but rather an aggression or an occupation from within. In other words, you legally speaking had no way of introducing these War Presidencies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Despite the warning from the bench, I believe that I need to make a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, you will not digress, Mr. Buntic. Let counsel ask you the questions and just answer them, please. It's a matter for this Trial Chamber to decide what is relevant and important here. As you've heard, this case has been going on a very long time. We've heard a very great deal of evidence. Now, counsel knows what the issues are, and he will ask you the relevant questions and could you kindly confine your answers to the questions. Mr. Naumovski, would you ask your question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I said, Mr. Buntic, provided that this was not a foreign aggression but rather an internal aggression, the attack was carried out by the JNA which was supposed to have protected the population. Legally speaking, there was no provision for introducing a War Presidency so that you Croats and also Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina established Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The municipal assemblies appointed the same persons to the Crisis Staffs which would have been appointed to the War Presidencies had they been able to establish them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: In most cases that was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And people from various political parties took part in these staffs. In other words, all the parliamentarian parties so to speak in --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, and some people based on their position, the president of the civilian protection, the president of the municipal council then the president of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless if these Crisis Staffs were established or not, the basic duty, the basic constitutional obligation of the municipality was to protect, to defend its own territory.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, this obligation issued both out of the SFRY constitution and the Bosnian constitution and the law of defence both federal and the republican, that is, all these documents were provided for this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of these documents have been provided in the Tab 8 of the bundle, especially the law on defence of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct? This was provided in paragraph 8.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through this internal aggression, there was a split between the old legal system which existed and the reality on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the legal system which was still in force at the time did not correspond to the reality of what actually had happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a split. According to some constitutional provisions, I have to say that the armed forces of the SFRY consisted of two components. One was the JNA and the other was the Territorial Defence. Part of the constitutional provisions obliged people to serve with the JNA but there were also duties to serve with the Territorial Defence and it -- and the municipalities also were obliged to set up defences of their own territories. So the federal and republican constitutions were now in collision as were the federal and republican law of defence and it resulted in a general legal chaos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you referred to the Territorial Defence, the Territorial Defence in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina was, for the most, part disarmed because the JNA took away the weapons which was legally owned by the republic, that is, the state municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, if one component of the armed forces disarmed the other component of the armed forces, it took away weapons which legally belonged to the municipalities and locally-based companies. It was clear how it was all going to end; that is, the attitude of the JNA towards its other component became very clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to conclude this topic, in short, the Croats and Muslims in the summer of 1991 set up Crisis Staffs and started to prepare against the aggression which was inevitable?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I would say that this job was finished by September where in all municipalities were Muslims and Croats were in the majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A while ago you mentioned that there was an absolute real and legal chaos in the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina primarily because there the work of all hitherto legal authorities was blocked; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: It is common knowledge that on the 15th of October 1992, the SDA [as interpreted] members left the parliament and did not come back to it so that the parliament of BH was completely blocked. And all the same thing happened with the assembly because the Serb representatives quit both the assembly and the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina so that it was impossible to convene sessions and take relevant decisions in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It means that all the legal institutions of the state were blocked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, we found this reflection not only among the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina but the overall legal life. This legal chaos, if I may call it that, did not however end up in anarchy because ways were sought to organise new institutions, different institutions, which would organise life not only across the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina but primarily in the individual municipality.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: One could define this as disorder, disarray. You cannot really call it anarchy. And when some institutions were blocked, the people looked for other institutions through which they could arrange civilian life in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not know if it was your slip of the tongue or the problem here. It was obvious that the members of the Serb Democratic Party left the parliament. It is page 14 line 6.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: And in the face of this unusual situation, all the sides begin to form their social institutions, that is HVO, then the Muslims formed the Patriotic League and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the legitimate legal state institutions were blocked in order to prevent general chaos in the society, new institutions were formed to regulate civilian life and ensure at least the minimum function of civilian life?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the military part was also formed so as to organise that duty, which is both, and the basic territories because of the attacks by the JNA and part of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I have already said that the Crisis Staff, that is, the military organisations were set up in municipalities with Croat and Muslim majorities sometime until the end of the -- September 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. We can move on to the information of the Croat Democratic Community of Herceg-Bosna, this is paragraph 19, Your Honours. The Chamber already knows, Mr. Buntic, that the Croat Community Bosanska Posavina was formed and then the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna was formed in Grude in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This decision was then amended in the session of the Presidency of the HZ HB on the 3rd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were some amendments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As head of the department for Justice and Administration, you participated in the sessions of the HZ HB and you were therefore present also at those fundamental crucial sessions which took a series of decisions and adopted various regulations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this session of the HZ HB Presidency held in July 1992, HZ HB was then set up as a kind of regional government within the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to resolve the problems that we just -- that we spoke about a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on one hand, its task was very briefly to ensure the conditions for a defence against the aggression and on the other, to ensure the minimum organisation of the other part, the civilian part of life?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: One needs to mention that between the 3rd of April 1992 until the 26th of -- 20th of June 1992, there was no electric power across Herzegovina, there was no water, there was no telephone lines; that is, they were cut off. There was food shortage, tremendous inflation, and somebody had to regulate those matters and ensure some minimal living conditions for those people so that -- so as to avoid an exodus of people from that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna began ever more active as the central authority weakened. The less efficient was the central government because the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina was falling apart, the more -- was the HDZ becoming more?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I should say until August of 1992, the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna passed almost no decisions nor did the civilian part show any signs of particular activity, and the institutions of the HZ HB began to be more animated as of latter August 1992 onwards, rather, after that session held on July 3rd when documents were signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us remind the Court it is the time when the Bosnian Serb army is already holding about 70 per cent of the territory of the then Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this evolution that you are talking about, the evolution of the HZ HB in October, that is, as of this session on the 17th of October, the things were then completely separated, that is, the civilian and the military part -- wing of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna parted company, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it was -- no. It is not perhaps. It is certainly a very unhappy choice of name, because HVO was the term of the -- for the military -- denoting military parts of the Croats there. And it was also decided that the civilian part of the HZ HB should be called the civilian HVO. But one must tell one thing from the other. There was the civilian part and its presidency, and we call it conditionally, perhaps, the government or the executive board of the Croats, that is, the presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, which needs to be distinguished from the Croat Defence Council, which was the name of the units of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, the Croats, in point of fact, by organising yourselves, tried to preserve the rights that you enjoyed also under the former constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Those rights were basically also the -- served as the basis for your political programme?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina is the state of three peoples, and that is clearly defined in the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, practically. There was an attempt to ensure an equal constitutional position of the status of Croats in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna was founded, it incorporated parts of 30 municipalities. In this case, as you know, it is alleged that HZ HB also incorporated some areas where the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have the majority.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct. These are the territories of some municipalities, but they are not whole municipalities. The decision on the foundation of the HZ HB refers to parts of some municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you prepared the summary, we discussed it because of the translation into English, and this word, "parts of territories," could also -- can be called differently. Parts of territories, of individual territories, that would make it more clear to understand, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it happened, and I believe we already had an opportunity of telling that to Their Honours because of the historical -- my colleague is also telling me that I also have to slow down a little bit. Thank you very much. Excuse me. It happened because of the historical custom of Serbs, if I may call it that, to organise municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina so as to always have Croats a minority in a municipality. So you gave us the example of Ravno, which was 100 per cent Croat, but because it was part of the municipality of Trebinje, there were only about 4 per cent of Croats in that municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the municipality of Ravno was annexed to the municipality of Trebinje, then -- and their -- the percentage of the Croats was only 4 per cent, even though before this annexation the municipality of Ravno had only 4 -- was a hundred per cent Croat. There are many other such examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are both being warned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, would you both slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Buntic, will you please help me not to speed too much, because the transcript will not be clear. And don't answer immediately, until my question has been interpreted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not in the transcript now. It doesn't have to be repeated. You agreed with me what I've just said, only you explained it further, but I really do not think we need to explain it particularly. Mr. Buntic, the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna incorporated parts of 30 municipalities with a Croat majority or in which one can organise defence efficiently?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were those areas where you had the majority or where you ranked the second in size?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I believe this was so in almost all the cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few words about the evolution of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, even though we've already said a word or two about that. When the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna was proclaimed on the 18th of November, 1991, it was a political organisation created to represent and protect, we could say so, the interest of Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is why it was founded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, a few months later, the Croat community was practically inactive for several months, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, as we have already said, as the central government weakened, so the internal organisation of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna grew. And during that evolution, first the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, in April 1992, set up the military organisation, that is, the military part of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct. On the 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then in May, that is, 15 May 1992, the civilian wing of the HVO was set up -- these are its beginnings -- when some civilian functions were gradually embarked upon.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: As I have said already, provisional executive authority was set up, that is, the executive part of the presidency of the HZ HB, called the Croat Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The meeting that was held on July 3rd, 1992, in point of fact reorganised the civilian and the military part, and following that the civilian wing began to operate as a provisional wartime regional authority under emergency conditions but within the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would call it provisional executive government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, within the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please. I do not want to lead you here, because there could be an objection. Was the foundation of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna a secret or was it publicised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: The founding of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna was commented by both the president of the HDZ at the time, Stjepan Kljuic, and then vice-president of the HDZ Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Mate Boban, a day or two after the foundation, and these comments were published in the paper Oslobodenje on the 20 -- no. I think one or two days after its proclamation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the exhibit that we attached to your summary, 2 and 3 include excerpts, fragments, from articles referring to the foundation of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna. These are articles from the press?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, these are articles from the paper called Oslobodenje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was -- we can't even speak about anything clandestine there. It was -- the founding of HZ HB was quite open. At that time Oslobodenje was the most widely read newspaper in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, at its session on the 28th of November, 1991, recognised the legitimacy of both the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna and the Croat Community of Bosanska Posavina; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And more than that, it also supported and made the initiative for other organisations to be set up in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: And it was also made possible for other municipalities to join, if they wished to do so, the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague warns me of something in the transcript. We said that the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina recognised the legitimacy of these Croat communities that I've just talked about.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's an imprecision in the transcript, so all I wanted was to correct that. So we are paragraph 29, the establishment of the armed forces. You've already explained that in part. And by and large, as the Court already knows, the military part of the HVO was set up on the 8th of April, 1992 as a provisional body, which then tried to coordinate the activities of the existing defence forces in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina formed until -- by that time already. However, there was a lack of coordination to bring them all together.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I have already pointed out that the municipal Crisis Staff had been set up before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When we spoke about this HVO, it was set up only as a provisional organisation, having to do with the war, with the imminent threat of war, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I think that all the documents adopted by the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna and the documents adopted by the HVO, every one of these documents has the wording to show that it is a document which is only temporarily in force during the threat of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In these territories in which it was formed, the task of the HVO was to defend whom? Only the Croats or all the citizens living there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Not only was it its task; it also provided that defence by and large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't understand you. All citizens or only the Croats?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: All citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So regardless of the ethnic, national, whatever, religious, or other difference?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: All without any difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've just mentioned the Territorial Defence; however, we did not say why did you Croats -- in fact were rather mistrustful of the Territorial Defence. Perhaps now is the time to say something about that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Territorial Defence in Bosnia-Herzegovina was a Serb. I think his name was Vasiljevic. And the paradox of the Territorial Defence is testified to by the fact that all the armaments were turned over to the other component, that is, the Yugoslav People's Army, and the fact that from the funds, from the resources of the Territorial Defence, Commander Vasiljevic paid the salaries of those in service who had occupied the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So that is, I believe, sufficient reason not to trust the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moreover, I think that in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina it was common knowledge that the TO was largely controlled by Serbs. That was the additional reason for this lack of confidence.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I think that that was the structure throughout the armed forces of the former Republic of Yugoslavia, that the military personnel was structured so that over 60 per cent of them were Serbs and Montenegrins and all the others accounted for the rest of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have given us some of the reasons for which you Croats believed that the TO could not defend successfully, protect the interests of the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Well, simply, the name was neither appropriate nor adequate for the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not in dispute that the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- the decision was signed by the then-president, Alija Izetbegovic, that it set up a new Territorial Defence on the 9th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, at that time the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not yet exist as such?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established only as late as the 6th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the bulk of the forces at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: The bulk of the forces were units called either Territorial Defence or the units called the Muslim Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these components, especially the Patriotic League, became the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Patriotic League, and the HVO, by a decision of the presidents of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 6th of August, were proclaimed to be the legal forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina defending the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can say equal parts of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us dwell for a while on this organisation of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna. The organisation took place at the session of the presidency of the HZ HB on the 3rd of July, 1992. The session, therefore, brought about the reorganisation and also introduced some temporary institutions which were not in existence before that. For instance, you set up new, if I may call it, supreme authority; you introduced the title of the president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the same time the president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna became the supreme commander of the armed forces; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, the supreme commander of all armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Court already knows that both these duties were discharged by Mate Boban. But tell us, please: Did Mate Boban, as the president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna and the supreme commander, have any vice-presidents, or is it that such a post did not exist?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No, the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna never had any vice-presidents. That post has to be distinguished from the role of the president of the Presidency of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is my second question. One of the decisions taken by the session on the 3rd of July 1992 was also the decision that the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna should grow into a fully legislative body, if I may call it that, of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a body which adopted regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna was headed by the president, and in this case, it was also Mr. Mate Boban except that the president of the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna had two vice-presidents; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: It is anything that the vice-presidents were then named, it was Mr. Dario Kordic, who is here, and Mr. Bozo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The duty of the president of the Presidency, and we have to emphasise the distinction between this duty and the president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna so his duties were of parliamentary nature, they were to translate into life the programme of the Croat Democratic Union and so on and so forth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I would say exclusively of a parliamentary nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are familiar with the provisions of the rules on the work of the Presidency adopted in October 1992; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are only two articles, the 15th and the 20th which briefly mention vice-presidents of the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna. Do they have any other duties apart from those parliamentary duties as we call them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to those rules, they have no other duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, vice-presidents of the president of the Presidency can substitute for the president. They can convene meetings and do things that have to do with the house rules and orders of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they can substitute for the president in his absence and they can help assist in preparation for the meetings of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to refer to Exhibit D181/1 paragraph three in that regard, and the last question Mr. Buntic in this paragraph three or heading three, sorry. D181/1, Tab 3. Does this position give any executive power within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 34. We're moving along, Your Honours. The Presidency met only two more times, we are talking about the HZ HB Presidency. Once was on 14 August 1992 and 17 October 1992. Both times in order to adopt significant legislation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the session of 17 October 1992, the Presidency of HZ HB transferred its legislative powers or they delegated it in instances that cannot be delayed -- I'm quoting you in paragraph 34 -- and to this executive body only for the duration of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. And after 17 October, the Presidency of HZ HB never passed any further legislation. The legislation was then adopted by the executive branch, that is, the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later -- earlier we talked about the session of 3 July 1992, the Presidency was created, that was the commander in chief of HVO, and I think you were denied the opportunity to say that this is when the main staff of the military HVO was established which was subordinated to the Presidency -- which was the commander in chief?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: With this revised, amended provision, the main staff was set up and the commander in chief, that is, the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was its superior commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, with the internal Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and initially we said all this was done in order to organise the entire life in Herceg-Bosna, we see that all these rules were conformed to the BiH constitution and laws?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: We tried to -- we tried to follow all the legislation, the -- that is, of the Bosnian and even the federal legislation insofar as it was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Amendment 42 of the BiH constitution adopted on 21 April 1989, municipalities could join together into a community of municipalities for certain purposes or needs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to the constitution and the law of defence, both allow the possibility for this kind of joinder for the purpose of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your outline in paragraph 36, you said that the RBiH Presidency itself concluded that new forms of governmental structures were needed outside Sarajevo and it created certain regional governments or districts, "Okruzi" in Croatian?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, such districts were created for the areas of Zenica, Tuzla and Bihac which was very similar to the internal organisation of Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was concluded that this was one of the most effective ways to organise local territorial units?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: There were no other possibilities because Sarajevo was cut off from these other urban centres; Mostar, Tuzla and Zenica, and because of the inability to maintain physical communication between these various regional centres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the evolution of this, the president of the HVO executive after May 15, 1992 was Mr. Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Initially there was a single vice-president. First it was Stipo Ivankovic, but in a session of 17 October 1992, the Presidency of the HZ HB appointed two additional vice-presidents, Kresimir Zubak and Anto Valenta?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few comments, Mr. Buntic, on the detached department of the RBiH in Mostar and, Your Honours, this is paragraph 38. Their Honours know that in July 1992, Presidents Tudjman and Izetbegovic held a meeting but after that meeting, you met with the RBiH Minister of Justice; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: That was less than a month after -- following that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber what was the purpose of this meeting, that is, as your -- as head of the justice department of the HZ HB with the republican Minister of Justice?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: The purpose of the meeting was the functioning of the judicial system in the conditions of war and with Sarajevo being cut off from the other centres, we were wondering how to set up the judicial system within the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we also talked about the detached department of the RBiH Supreme Court in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This meeting did not result in any written agreement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, because at that time, the minister was not authorised to sign any documents on the agreement reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But during the discussions you held, was it agreed that it was absolutely necessary to set up these -- the departments of the Supreme Court not only in Mostar but in other towns in Bosnia-Herzegovina so that the legal system, judicial system could operate at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: The best proof is what the government of the RBiH did, that is, its Presidency. Shortly thereafter, detached departments were established in Bihac and Tuzla because Sarajevo was cut off and so these departments were established in Mostar and Tuzla and Bihac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may remind you, there was one also established in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these newly-established departments worked on equal footing with the one in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: They were all departments of the RBiH Supreme Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can further clarify this issue. The judges elected to the departments in Tuzla Bihac, Mostar, and Zenica, to whom they were giving oath, to what the representative of which body?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: It would be the head of the district. If it was in Tuzla, the president to the Tuzla district, and if it was in Bihac, it was at the head of the Bihac district.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these districts were -- are the new territorial units set up based on the model of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: We can say only conditionally this was set up by the HZ HB but it was similar, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to conclude this topic both Croats and Muslims in the territory which they controlled were forced to establish such departments because they were unable to communicate in Sarajevo where the republican Supreme Court had its seat?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that was the main reason why this solution was offered because there was no other way to implement the legal system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can move on to the next topic, that is the RBiH Constitutional Court decision on the unconstitutionality of the HZ HB. Your Honours, we are moving to paragraph 39. Mr. Buntic, you are aware that there were witnesses here who gave evidence that HZ HB was proclaimed unconstitutional in a decision of 14 September 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, as head of the HVO department of justice, did you ever receive any notice or were you ever offered an opportunity to take part in these proceedings in this RBiH Constitutional Court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been notified and had you had an opportunity to come to Sarajevo, would you have, in this session, represented -- your side, that is, the HZ HB as the head of its justice department?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, had that been possible, that is, to come to Sarajevo which I very much doubt was possible at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you or any other official of the HVO ever received an official copy of the decision of the RBiH Supreme Court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No, we never received an invitation to take part in this debate or the decision which was rendered as a result of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Naumovski, please. In relation to paragraph 39 with regard to the Constitutional Court, I'd like to put the following question to Mr. Buntic because, after all, he is an experienced lawyer and he was the lawyer within the civilian wing of the HVO. Could it be that he never had the opportunity to hear about the creation of a Constitutional Court because a decision relating to the creation of a Constitutional court could not to be compared with secondary courts, usually such a decision will have some major repercussions on political life. So does that mean that he didn't hear of the decision being adopted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: It is correct that I had not heard that -- that had I not heard that such a decision has been passed. I spent with Mr. Trnka in Neum, spent three days discussing the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he was a member of this body. I talked to the judicial branch and this decision was never mentioned to me. I had contacts with judges of the Supreme Court Drasko Vuleta and Mirko Pogdanovic and no one ever told me personally that such decision existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you never received information from another source, have you, it may be that these people didn't speak to you directly, but have you heard about it from another source just because it was public knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I heard about this decision in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, between 1992, yes, indeed, 1992, from the 14th of September 1992 until 1996. So for four years you never heard about it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's very surprising given that you were involved in legal matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, perhaps we can take this a step further based on what His Honour Judge Bennouna just asked. Insofar as you know as the head of the justice department, did anyone ever ask that this decision of the Supreme Court be implemented?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I'm unaware of any such activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this context, the persons with whom you later spoke not only did not tell you about this decision but never asked you to have this decision implemented.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I said that I learned about this decision in 1996 when we were first in a position to receive official gazettes from RBiH, and having received copies of these -- of the official gazette, I learned about it and I am sure that had anybody wanted it known that this decision was adopted, that they would have disseminated this information but I'm unaware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having -- I would just like to refer to the bundle, it is the pertinent portions of the constitution and that is the provision of the constitutional provisions and the rules of Supreme Court of BiH with its amendments are in Tabs 6 and 7.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these regulations regulate the issues which we have just addressed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of the judicial system, the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina confirmed certain decisions of the HVO on the appointments of judges to courts within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, that is, until this decision of the unconstitutionality.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I believe that there were certain confirmations adopted even after this decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to refer you to Tabs 4 and 5 of the exhibit we have introduced. One is a decision of the Presidency of the 23rd of August of the election of judges of the military -- district military courts and somewhere in the middle, there are -- there is a list of judges appointed to the district military court in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the decision in Tab 5 is a decision of the RBiH Presidency of 7 September 1992, and in Roman numeral VIII paragraph, there are appointments of the judges in the higher court in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Just in conclusion, were these judges elected or appointed to positions in courts of the HZ HB confirmed by the Presidency of RBiH?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, as an experienced legal expert and lawyer, I think that you would be the right person to know and ask this, even to date, the federation courts still apply and implement the regulations adopted by the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Precisely, all regulations of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna/HZH-B/ are being applied which have not been replaced by federal regulations. So all the regulations adopted by the HZH-B are treated equally to the regulations adopted by the BH Republic. So the supreme court does not make any distinction between the laws which had been passed by the HZ HB and the ones which were adopted by the Federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is a lawyer. He might be in a position to explain why such legislation, such laws, are being applied, because it often happens that law is applied in order to avoid a legal vacuum. Until such law can be replaced by another type of legislation, this often happens. There are even cases when independent states keep applying, for instance, colonial legislation, in order to avoid a legal vacuum. But that doesn't mean, by doing so, that they do admit or acknowledge a colonisation. However, they do apply colonial rules or laws because they want to avoid a legal vacuum. Is it here the purpose -- do you want to avoid some kind of legal vacuum, and was it done in order to -- by applying the previous legislation to Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: It is correct that Herceg-Bosna implemented the regulations both of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the regulations of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But in the areas where it had jurisdiction which were affected by the war, it had to legislate there. And even to date, even as we are meeting today, if no new federal legislation had been introduced, there is still old laws that are being implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are not answering my question, Mr. Buntic. My question was: They are applied, there are in force these laws of Herceg-Bosna in order to avoid a legal vacuum; is that the reason? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, can you please tell us whether the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, that is, the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, were ever supposed to be internationally recognised entities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the very beginning of the establishment of the HZ HB, what did the basic documents all refer to? What supreme authority was to be recognised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: In all -- all documents adopted by the HZ HB always stipulated that these were provisional documents in the conditions of war, that it is an entity that is going to persist so long as there was the war or immediate threat of war. It never had an ambition to become an independent state and never asked for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose supreme authority was to be recognised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: That of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me now: The Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and all other citizens of the HZ HB, were they citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina or were they citizens of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, as was sometimes -- it was sometimes contended here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: There is no document that reflects that position of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you were all only the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any official border crossings between the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the areas controlled by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No. There were no official border crossings, and this is also reflected in all the documents adopted by the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a feeling that we have made good progress, but perhaps we can fit in another few questions. This is paragraphs 45, 46, relations between the Republic of Croatia and the HZ HB. As Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you ever consider the constitution of the Republic of Croatia as your supreme law?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could such a law have any legal force in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other parts of the legal system of the Republic of Croatia -- and I refer to the supreme court and other bodies -- have any influence on the legal system within Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the head of the justice department until 28 August 1993, until the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was established. Can you tell me whether the HZ HB in that period ever applied, implemented, any piece of legislation of the Croatian Republic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any meetings with any officials from the justice department of Croatia with whom you discussed the legislation in HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I never met with the head of the justice department of the Republic of Croatia, either officially or unofficially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later on, when in December 1993 you became -- you assumed your new duty, did you, in your new position, have any meetings or contacts with representatives of the judiciary of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No. I never officially or unofficially met with the president of the judicial council of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last question from this -- on this topic. As the head of the justice department, did you ever receive any orders or suggestions from the Republic of Croatia what you should do in your job?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: If we never met, then I never could have received any such orders or suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this may be a good moment to take a break before we go on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's 11.00. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Buntic, would you remember in this adjournment, and any others there may be, not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include members of the Defence team. Could you be back, please, at half past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, we've reached paragraph 47.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, we can continue. Tell us, please: Was there any policy, plan, law, regulation, anything in the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna or the HVO which would expose any ethnic group to any kind of persecution or discrimination?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I do not know of any such plan. I know that there was no such regulation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the duty that you discharged, you practically socialised with all the people who meant something in the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there existed any secret or real plan about some systematic persecution or discrimination, persecution or discrimination of Muslims, of others, of non-Croats, wouldn't you know about that, either officially or from contacts with people who took the most important decisions in the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I would have known, had it existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had such a plan existed, would you ever have been a person to put such plans through?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please: Was the objective of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna the creation of any ethnically homogeneous territory?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it, at any decision-making level that you attended, either in the HVO government or anything, was there ever any mention about resettlements within the HZ HB of any people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, if in the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna there was a plan or was -- or did it happen in practice that Muslims were excluded from government at any level?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you well, there was no plan to create a monoethnic state, in inverted commas, "state," of course.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned an interesting fact in your summary in paragraph 48 whereas there was some clashes between the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in some parts of Bosnia, in Tuzla, Bihac and other places, in other places, they fought jointly against the aggressor, that is, the army of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, even that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us a while ago that there was no discrimination of Muslims by the authorities but you also meant the judiciary, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: In the first place in the sector for which I was responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A certain number of judges were Muslims, even Serbs and even some other peoples not counting Croats, of course, were also judges and presidents of courts in courts which operated in the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: In Mostar, there was quite a number of -- there was a larger number of judges of Muslim ethnicity than Croat judges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 49 you give us some examples, for instance, Mr. Semir Puzic was a judge and also the president of this department detachment of the Supreme Court in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Enes Memic was the president of the military court in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also quoted the example of Mrs. Ziba Nozic who was the president of the municipal court in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all told, even your deputy, Aid Glavovic was a Muslim and he was responsible for the punishment policy. So without going any further, these are the examples for which you draw the conclusion that there was no discrimination against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct. In addition to these Bosniaks mentioned here, the Serbs who had stayed back in Mostar and had been judges before that continued as such so nobody was dismissed from his office of the judge because of his ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course since some Serb judges and other people left, quit, left the areas of the HZ HB, there were a number of vacancies in the judiciary?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, by and large because until 1991, these places were held by people of Serb ethnicity. In Mostar and in Herzegovina, Serbs had a disproportionately large number of posts compared with the number of the population of that ethnicity living in the region and, naturally, when a large number of those judges left, one had to fill those vacancies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did that by -- after, of course, people applied for these posts for the Croat applicants, you requested some consent of the civilian HVO and for the Muslims, you requested the consent of the Muslim side, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was after such consents were given that you decided on the appointment of those applicants to different posts as judges?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Well, the proposal then went to the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna and the Presidency was the one which appointed judges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last part in this part of your examination, and these are the official positions and powers of Dario Kordic. We have practically touched upon both of his duties but let us just clarify it. In the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna according to your knowledge, as you told us, he held two posts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, he was the vice-president of the Presidency of Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We do not have to repeat the difference between the president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna and the president of the Presidency of Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna as indicated in paragraph 51A. Perhaps just in one word, the duties, the powers of the vice-president of the Presidency of the HZ HB were of parliamentary nature as we have already said.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have already said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And together with you as one of the five members, Mr. Dario Kordic was a member of the personnel commission of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already told us that this commission never sat in practice, and that you don't know of any decisions that it took.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall a single meeting of that commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, as the vice-president of the Presidency of Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, was Mr. Kordic also one of numerous members of the legislative body, that is the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna which was the decision-making body as we have already said?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the Presidency and one of the vice-presidents of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to explain to Their Honours, prior to the adoption of those fundamental rules and regulations, it was until the 17th of October 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Indeed, after that date, the Presidency did not adopt regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, if Mr. Kordic, as a vice-president of the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna as one of the members of this legislative body, did he have any powers to intervene in military matters, in judicial cases or any other walk of life? Did he have any such powers as a member of these bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have already said that the president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mate Boban, did not have his deputy as such.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is paragraph 53 where you said that it is important to emphasise which office Mr. Kordic did not hold. So Mr. Kordic was the vice-president of the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna but not the vice-president to the president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct. The president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna did not have a deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the head of the department for justice, did you ever hear in these sessions of this body of the HVO or in your private contacts with various individuals, did you ever hear that Mr. Kordic held any military duty or position or a role?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Kordic was not a member of the main staff. Also, I never heard that he was a member of the operative staff for Central Bosnia, military, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But did you ever hear that regardless of the fact that he was not a member of these bodies that you mentioned, did you ever hear that he discharged any military function in any capacity whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I have already said that he was not a member of any of these staffs. Likewise, in the executive part, Mr. Kordic did not participate, so he did not participate in the executive bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps just one more question in this regard. Did Mr. Kordic ever participate in the design of the strategic policy during the life of Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna except as a member of that body which was responsible for the adoption of regulations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: I did not hear about any such activity of his.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, we are talking about these relations and relationships. Did Mr. Kordic, as the vice-president of the Presidency of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, was he superior to the president of the HVO, Dr. Jadranko Prlic, either de juro de facto?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he your superior as one of the heads of the departments of that government as it is colloquially called?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kordic have any duty in that executive body Croat Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: No. He was a member of this commission, and we have already noted that it never met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this leads us to one of our final questions. Did he ever, to your knowledge, participate in decision-making at the highest level, I mean, in the highest ranking institutions of the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Except in the Presidency that we have already spoken about, he did not take part in government sessions or any executive bodies, that is, I do not know that he attended any such meetings of the HVO. I'm referring to the executive part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have already told Their Honours that the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna was increasingly developing its organisation with the weakening of the central authority and that, I guess, means that in cooperation of ever larger people in the territory covered by Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within that context, did the office which Mr. Kordic held until 28th of August, 1993, that is, vice-president or deputy of the president of the Presidency of the HZ HB, did his role increase or decrease in view of the increase of the number of people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: In relation to the executive part and all that that we talked about, no, I think it was -- that it decreased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps my last question, Mr. Buntic, you have already told Their Honours that neither the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna nor the Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna were to become independent entities but only parts of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were the head of the department of justice in those hard critical county times, as you told us, in the territory of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, you, as you told us, enforced a whole range of laws in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which were already in effect for some time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Yes. In practical terms, all the laws of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina remained in force except that we made some amendments as to the terms and similar things in view of the circumstances that prevailed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question: You have already told us the decisions that you took in the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna referred to its provisional nature within the system of the Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
utterances.text: Indeed, all these regulations say that there are provisional documents in force during the threat of war and the imminent danger of war, and that they make part of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question: The enforcement of laws adopted by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, its decisions and so on so forth, is also an example testifying to the fact that you Croats recognise the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC
